content.title: World Baseball Classic: Venezuela takes down Team USA in championship game stunner
content.text: Once again, the final of the World Baseball Classic delivered a game worth remembering. This time, it was Venezuela breaking through against Team USA, with a win bound to resonate throughout the country.The Venezuelans defeated the United States 3-2 on Tuesday in Miami, capping off a tournament that showcased baseball at its best. Tears were flowing as soon as Venezuela closer Daniel Palencia’s fastball reached the glove of Salvador Perez for the final out.AdvertisementThe title is Venezuela’s first in six incarnations of the WBC, joining the U.S., Japan and the Dominican Republic as winners. Venezuela had to face all three in this tournament, losing to the D.R. in pool play before recovering with a comeback win over Japan in the quarterfinals.[Yahoo Fantasy Bracket Mayhem: Make your picks for $50K in total prizes] The final was a victory that took fortitude from Venezuela, which held a 2-0 lead in the eighth inning, only to lose it on an electric, game-tying home run from Bryce Harper. With a fresh ballgame and an inning to go, Venezuela regrouped.And then Eugenio Suárez put his team back on top.AdvertisementOn the defensive side, it took an incredible performance from a gassed Venezuela pitching staff to keep a stacked Team USA lineup under thumb.Hero performances from Venezuelan pitching staffIf there was extra reason for Team USA to be confident entering the game, it was the state of Venezuela’s pitchers.The starting pitcher was Eduardo Rodríguez, who holds a 5.02 ERA over the past two MLB seasons. Venezuela’s bullpen had been its biggest strength of knockout play but also had to cover 7 2/3 innings against Italy in the semifinal on Monday. Venezuela manager Omar López said before the final that he woke up Tuesday to three text messages from MLB organizations telling him not to use their relievers on back-to-back nights.AdvertisementIt’s unclear if those requests were honored, but this was clearly one way the deck was stacked for Team USA, whose bullpen was rested and largely ready to go after defeating the Dominican Republic on Sunday. Venezuela, meanwhile, had to figure out how to face a lineup in which the No. 9 hitter, Byron Buxton, was a 2025 MLB All-Star.Rodríguez took the mound and didn’t blink. Over 4 1/3 innings, he kept the Americans off-balance and exited with only one hit allowed and one walk against four strikeouts. Two of those were at the expense of Team USA captain Aaron Judge, who finished the night 0-for-4 with three strikeouts.Eduard Bazardo, José Buttó and Angel Zerpa combined for 2 1/3 scoreless innings after that. Then Andrés Machado entered needing to get four outs to deliver a 2-0 lead to Palencia. That’s when the hiccup in the plan arrived, as Harper punished a center-cut changeup to finally give Team USA some juice.AdvertisementThat could have been the first blow of a thrilling comeback for the United States, but it wasn’t. Machado got out of the inning, and Luis Arraez led off the ninth with a walk. He was replaced with pinch-runner Javier Sanoja, who barely pulled off a steal of second base.Then Suárez struck, Palencia got through the bottom of the ninth with no trouble, and the celebrations began. The Venezuelans were so dominant throughout the night that Team USA didn’t have a single at-bat with a runner in scoring position.Venezuela was pure joyIt can be so easy to disregard the WBC as an MLB-created entity designed to deliver easy-bake ratings in March and in which teams are overruled by MLB organizations on pitcher usage. But all of this so clearly matters to the players on the field and the fans behind them.AdvertisementThroughout the 2026 WBC, Venezuela’s fans stood out as one of the loudest groups, and they were the more audible presence in the stands for a final held on U.S. soil.It goes without saying that teams on the field want to win, but the moment was visibly washing over the Venezuelan players as they celebrated. It was clearly one of the greatest days of their lives — and that’s what you play for.Salvador Perez said after the game, “Now I feel like I can retire.” The longtime Kansas City Royals catcher wasn’t on the field when his team won the 2015 World Series, having been replaced for a pinch-runner, but he was behind the plate for this achievement.AdvertisementUSA-Venezuela has meaning beyond baseballIt is also a victory with an unavoidable political side. President Donald Trump poked Venezuela about the country becoming the 51st state via social media after its win over Italy on Monday and appeared to do so again immediately after the final pitch Tuesday. Suárez, the hero of the night, had his United States citizenship application canceled in December by Trump’s administration. And the game was held only a couple of months after the U.S. government removed Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro from the country.As much as these things can go unsaid in the world of baseball, it’s difficult to imagine that context wasn't on the minds of many Venezuelans entering Tuesday.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for news, updates and highlights from the World Baseball Classic final.Live coverage is over74 updatesWed, March 18, 2026 at 3:02 AM UTCWed, March 18, 2026 at 3:43 AM UTCWed, March 18, 2026 at 3:33 AM UTCWed, March 18, 2026 at 3:32 AM UTCMaikel Garcia is the World Baseball Classic MVP.He finished the tournament with 10 hits, including 1 home run, 7 RBI and 3 stolen bases.Wed, March 18, 2026 at 3:11 AM UTCWed, March 18, 2026 at 3:10 AM UTCWed, March 18, 2026 at 2:55 AM UTCRoman Anthony strikes out, and Venezuela wins the World Baseball Classic.Palencia finishes the job and tosses his glove to the sky, having shut down the USA bats to seal his country’s first tournament title.Team USA’s offense was nearly absent in this game, aside from Bryce Harper’s home run, and the Americans will head back to spring training with a lot of regrets and what-ifs.Wed, March 18, 2026 at 2:53 AM UTCGunnar Henderson pops out, and Team USA is down to its very last out.It’ll be up to Roman Anthony.Wed, March 18, 2026 at 2:51 AM UTCDaniel Palencia is on the mound to close this out for Venezuela.He gets Schwarber swinging for out No. 1.Wed, March 18, 2026 at 2:51 AM UTCAfter an intentional walk to Abreu, Salvador Perez flies out.On to the bottom of the ninth.
